bib.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Pretext-Invariant Representations
bib.venue: CVPR 2020 (arXiv v1 Dec 2019; Facebook AI Research)

question: Can self-supervised image representations be improved by making them invariant to the pretext transformation instead of covariant with it?
hypothesis: Semantic representations ought to be invariant under image transformations, so a contrastive invariance loss on a pretext task should beat predicting transformation properties.
contributions: PIRL: a contrastive loss that makes the representation of an image similar to that of its transformed version and dissimilar to other images
Applied to Jigsaw and Rotation pretext tasks, with state-of-the-art self-supervised results on several benchmarks
Outperforms supervised ImageNet pre-training for object detection

method.summary: A ResNet-50 is trained with an NCE loss (convex combination, lambda) between an image I and its pretext-transformed version I^t (Jigsaw: nine patches shuffled; also Rotation), using a memory bank of 32,000 negatives as in NPID. Representations are then evaluated by linear probes, finetuned detection, and semi-supervised finetuning.

datasets.name: ImageNet-1k train (no labels)
datasets.preprocessing: random resized crop, flip, photometric jitter; no Fast AutoAugment

datasets.name: YFCC-1M
datasets.size: 1M images randomly selected from the 100M YFCC

datasets.name: ImageNet / Places205 / iNaturalist2018 / VOC07
datasets.split: linear probes; ImageNet validation single/center crop

datasets.name: VOC07+12 train (16K images) and VOC07 train+val (5K), VOC07 test

models.name: PIRL ResNet-50
models.architecture: ResNet-50; res5 avg-pooled (2048-d) then linear head to 128-d; Jigsaw head g: 9 patches each res5 pooled -> linear 128-d, concatenated (1152-d) -> linear 128-d

models.name: PIRL-c2x
models.architecture: ResNet-50 with doubled channels per stage

models.name: NPID++
models.architecture: PIRL with lambda=0 (NPID with more negatives and epochs)

training.objective: Noise contrastive loss L = lambda*L_NCE(m_I, g(v_It)) + (1-lambda)*L_NCE(m_I, f(v_I)); memory bank m_I EMA of f(v_I), weight 0.5; cosine similarity; tau=0.07; lambda=0.5; N=32,000 negatives
training.regularisation: data augmentation: random resized crop, flip, color jitter etc.

other.jigsaw_input: crop >=60% of image resized to 255x255, 3x3 grid, 64x64 patch each, photometric aug per patch; I is 224x224
other.linear_probe: features avg-pooled to ~9,000 dims; SGD lr 0.01 decayed 0.1 twice, momentum 0.9, wd 5e-4; 28 epochs ImageNet, 14 Places205, 84 iNat; linear SVMs for VOC07
other.detection: Faster R-CNN C4 Detectron2, 8 GPUs x 2 images; VOC07+12: 25K iters, lr dropped 0.1 at 17K; VOC07: 12.5K iters, drop at 9.5K; PIRL/NPID++ lr 0.003 warmup 1000 iters, supervised/Jigsaw lr 0.02 warmup 100; BatchNorm fixed

inference.samples: single run reported; no seeds or error bars

metrics.name: top-1 accuracy
metrics.definition: linear classifier on frozen features of best layer; single/center crop

eval.protocol: Transfer-learning evaluation following Goyal et al. 2019 (best layer per method); numbers for PIRL, NPID++, Rotation obtained by the authors, others adopted from papers.

limits: Evaluated on ImageNet-scale ResNet-50 only; gains shrink against concurrent MoCo (55.2 APall, 60.6 top-1) which the paper notes is concurrent work.
Single runs, no seeds or error bars; PIRL AP50 on VOC07 below supervised (73.4 vs 74.5).
Ablations (Sec 4) use 400 epochs and N=4,096, so absolute numbers are lower; lambda, N and |T| results are shown only as plots.
Table 5 PIRL (Jigsaw) 62.2 differs from Table 2 63.6 without explanation.
Authors concede PIRL is sensitive to lambda.
Compute hardware type and wall clock not stated; MoCo-comparison conditions differ (BatchNorm finetuned).
